topic_title: Chapter 4 - Lesson 4-3 - Methods for Evaluating Websites

questions.question: Qualitative evaluation mainly uses numerical data to understand how much something is happening.
PV represents the number of times a page has been viewed.
Bounce rate is the proportion of visits that ended after viewing only the first page.
Heuristic evaluation uses experts who identify UI problems using rules of thumb.
What type of evaluation helps explain why a website problem occurs?
For each method, choose A Qualitative or B Quantitative.

items.text: Users explore the website and their usability is observed.
Access counts and page views are tallied.
Users are interviewed about their impressions and improvement requests.
Numerical website data is analyzed to understand overall trends.

questions.question: Match each description with the correct indicator: A PV, B Bounce rate, C CVR.

items.text: Total number of times a page has been viewed.
Proportion of visits ending after the first page.
Proportion of visits achieving a target action such as purchase or registration.

questions.question: Which most appropriately describes heuristic evaluation?
options: Users explore the site and usability is observed.
Experts identify UI problems based on rules of thumb.
Two patterns are prepared and compared using data.

questions.question: An online bookstore has high PV but very low CVR. What does this most likely indicate?
options: Few people are visiting the website.
Many people visit, but few take the target action.

questions.question: A school website gets many visits, but most users leave after the first page. Name one quantitative indicator, one qualitative method to find the cause, and one possible improvement.
questions.model_answer: The bounce rate is a suitable quantitative indicator. Usability testing or interviews can help find the cause. A possible improvement would be to improve the first-page information or navigation based on the findings.
